title: How our brain makes sense of a noisy world, with Nina Kraus, PhD

sentences.en: Music, conversation, bird song, a truck backing up, the hum of a refrigerator, the leaf blower across the street.
sentences.zh: 音乐、谈话、鸟鸣、倒车的卡车声、冰箱的嗡嗡声、街对面的吹叶机声。

sentences.en: We live in a world of constant, complex sound, yet most of us don't spend very much time thinking about the role that sound plays in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个充满持续、复杂声音的世界里，但我们大多数人并没有花太多时间去思考声音在我们生活中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Polls find that most people, when asked to rank their senses, value sight the highest with hearing a distant second.
sentences.zh: 民意调查显示，当被要求对感官进行排名时，大多数人认为视觉最重要，听觉则排在遥远的第二位。

sentences.en: But sound is integral to our lives, even to our mental health, and no two people's sonic world is exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 但声音对我们的生活，甚至对我们的心理健康都至关重要，而且没有两个人的声音世界是完全相同的。

sentences.en: Our life experiences shape the way that our brain processes sound, and sound is deeply intertwined with everything from our ability to read to our cognitive health as we age.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活经历塑造了大脑处理声音的方式，而声音与我们的一切息息相关，从我们的阅读能力到我们年老时的认知健康。

sentences.en: So why is sound so undervalued, especially by those of us who can hear?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么声音被如此低估，尤其是被我们这些有听力的人所低估呢？

sentences.en: How does our brain turn sound waves into brain waves?
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑是如何将声波转化为脑波的？

sentences.en: Do the brains of musicians differ from those of non-musicians?
sentences.zh: 音乐家的大脑与非音乐家的大脑有何不同？

sentences.en: Why is sound crucial to reading?
sentences.zh: 为什么声音对阅读至关重要？

sentences.en: Do other animals experience sound in the same way that humans do?
sentences.zh: 其他动物体验声音的方式和人类一样吗？

sentences.en: How does unwanted noise affect our ears and our brain?
sentences.zh: 不想要的噪音如何影响我们的耳朵和大脑？

sentences.en: Why does our hearing change as we age?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的听力会随着年龄的增长而改变？

sentences.en: And what can all of us do to create a better, healthier sonic world?
sentences.zh: 我们所有人又能做些什么来创造一个更好、更健康的声音世界呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Nina Krauss, director of the Auditory Neuroscience Lab, also called BrainVolts, at Northwestern University.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是西北大学听觉神经科学实验室（也称为 BrainVolts）的主任尼娜·克劳斯博士。

sentences.en: She's a scientist, inventor, and amateur musician who studies many aspects of auditory learning.
sentences.zh: 她是一位科学家、发明家和业余音乐家，研究听觉学习的多个方面。

sentences.en: The list of her research topics includes music, concussion, bilingualism, reading, aging, and autism.
sentences.zh: 她的研究课题包括音乐、脑震荡、双语、阅读、衰老和自闭症等。

sentences.en: She has invented new ways to measure sound processing in humans and has conducted studies in traditional research labs, as well as in schools, community centers, and clinics.
sentences.zh: 她发明了测量人类声音处理的新方法，并在传统研究实验室、学校、社区中心和诊所开展了研究。

sentences.en: She is the author of hundreds of peer-reviewed research articles and speaks frequently to the media about sound and the brain.
sentences.zh: 她是数百篇同行评审研究文章的作者，并经常向媒体谈论声音与大脑的相关话题。

sentences.en: Her recent book is called Of Sound Mind, How Our Brain Constructs a
sentences.zh: 她最近出版的书名为《有声思维：我们的大脑如何构建一个》

sentences.en: Meaningful Sonic World.
sentences.zh: “有意义的声音世界”。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me, Dr. Krauss.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我的节目，克劳斯博士。

sentences.en: I'm so glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: So a moment ago, I mentioned that people tend to rate sight as their most valued sense far ahead of hearing.
sentences.zh: 刚才我提到，人们倾向于将视觉视为他们最珍视的感官，远高于听觉。

sentences.en: Why do you think that hearing is so much less valued?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么听觉受到的重视程度要低得多？

sentences.en: Well, for one, it's invisible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它是隐形的。

sentences.en: And what we can see is right in front of us.
sentences.zh: 我们能看到的东西就在我们面前。

sentences.en: What we can hear actually is all around us, 360 degrees.
sentences.zh: 而我们能听到的声音实际上环绕着我们，是 360 度的。

sentences.en: But we live in a visually biased world.
sentences.zh: 但我们生活在一个视觉偏向的世界里。

sentences.en: And I think also as time is going on, we're forgetting how to listen and how important hearing is.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为随着时间的推移，我们正在忘记如何倾听，以及听觉有多么重要。

sentences.en: Sound very much connects us.
sentences.zh: 声音在很大程度上连接着我们。

sentences.en: It connects us with others.
sentences.zh: 它将我们与他人联系起来。

sentences.en: It connects us with the world in a way that is really different from the way we are connected with our other senses.
sentences.zh: 它以一种与我们通过其他感官连接方式截然不同的方式，将我们与世界联系起来。

sentences.en: Sound is evolutionarily ancient sound processing in the brain, really derived from primitive organisms, from cells that would move with vibration.
sentences.zh: 声音在进化上是古老的大脑声音处理机制，实际上源于原始生物，源于那些会随振动而移动的细胞。

sentences.en: And eventually in vertebrates, we have a complex auditory pathway.
sentences.zh: 最终在脊椎动物中，我们拥有了复杂的听觉通路。

sentences.en: But the fundamentals of hearing and the vibrations that we are able to discern and that any organism can discern is evolutionarily ancient and biologically important.
sentences.zh: 但听觉的基本原理，以及我们能够辨别、任何生物都能辨别的振动，在进化上是古老的，在生物学上是重要的。

sentences.en: Now, you spend the first third of your book explaining the basics of how sound works, how the ear and the brain convert waves, sound waves into brain activity.
sentences.zh: 你花了书的前三分之一来解释声音运作的基础知识，即耳朵和大脑如何将波、声波转化为大脑活动。

sentences.en: What makes sound unique in terms of how it's processed in the brain?
sentences.zh: 就大脑的处理方式而言，是什么让声音变得独特？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, even though light, the speed of light is faster than the speed of sound, the way we process sound in the brain is faster.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，尽管光速比声速快，但我们大脑处理声音的方式更快。

sentences.en: And if you can imagine, so right now as we're having this conversation, sound waves are occurring.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下，就在我们进行这次对话时，声波正在产生。

sentences.en: And within every sound wave, there is a tremendous amount of information that is happening in time, it's here and then it's gone.
sentences.zh: 在每一个声波中，都有大量的信息在时间中发生，它转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: It only is present for a second or for a millisecond, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，它只存在一秒钟或一毫秒。

sentences.en: And whereas what we see is something that is much more stable in terms of timing so that the timing requirements are going to be different.
sentences.zh: 而我们所看到的在时间上要稳定得多，所以时间要求是不同的。

sentences.en: The brain needs to make sense of sound.
sentences.zh: 大脑需要理解声音。

sentences.en: Similarly to how we make sense of a visual object, there are many ingredients that we right away are able to discern, you know, what is the shape, the size, the color,
sentences.zh: 就像我们理解视觉对象一样，我们能够立即辨别出许多要素，比如形状、大小、颜色，

sentences.en: how heavy is it?
sentences.zh: 它有多重？

sentences.en: And with sound, remember sound, first of all, is invisible.
sentences.zh: 对于声音，记住声音首先是隐形的。

sentences.en: And all of the ingredients are also invisible, but they are there.
sentences.zh: 所有的成分也都是隐形的，但它们确实存在。

sentences.en: So if we give it a thought, we realize that sound consists of pitch, how high or low the sound is.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们思考一下，就会意识到声音由音高组成，即声音的高低。

sentences.en: It consists of timbre.
sentences.zh: 它由音色组成。

sentences.en: Timbre is determined by the harmonics in sound.
sentences.zh: 音色由声音中的谐波决定。

sentences.en: Timbre is what allows us to tell the difference between two different instruments that are playing the same note.
sentences.zh: 音色使我们能够区分演奏同一个音符的两种不同乐器。

sentences.en: The harmonics enable us to distinguish one consonant from another, a ga from a ba.
sentences.zh: 谐波使我们能够区分一个辅音和另一个辅音，比如“ga”和“ba”。

sentences.en: There is so much timing, I mean, in every single waveform.
sentences.zh: 每一个波形中都有太多的时间信息。

sentences.en: And Kim, you know, you are actually looking at these waveforms and you can see how they stop and start and how they have so many timing
sentences.zh: 金，你知道，你实际上是在观察这些波形，你可以看到它们如何停止和开始，以及它们有多少时间

sentences.en: elements that the brain needs to make sense of.
sentences.zh: 要素是大脑需要去理解的。

sentences.en: So the brain is processing pitch, timing, timbre, phase, other ingredients with microsecond precision.
sentences.zh: 所以大脑正在以微秒级的精度处理音高、时间、音色、相位和其他成分。

sentences.en: And the signal, the sonic signal, the sound wave requires that that be done.
sentences.zh: 而信号，声音信号，声波要求必须这样做。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about the connection between sound and language, especially reading.
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈声音与语言，特别是阅读之间的联系。

sentences.en: People tend to think of reading as a visual activity, but your research has shown that sound is critical to our ability to read.
sentences.zh: 人们倾向于认为阅读是一种视觉活动，但你的研究表明声音对我们的阅读能力至关重要。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's not just my research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不仅仅是我的研究。

sentences.en: There really has been decades of research showing that sound is critical to the ability to read.
sentences.zh: 几十年的研究确实表明声音对阅读能力至关重要。

sentences.en: So why is that?
sentences.zh: 那么这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: We, you know, we learn to speak before we learn to read.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在学习阅读之前先学习说话。

sentences.en: And again, if we draw an evolution, think about the fact that we have been speaking and using sound for hundreds of thousands of years for communication.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果我们追溯进化，想想我们几十万年来一直通过说话和使用声音进行交流的事实。

sentences.en: We've only been reading for the past 3000 years.
sentences.zh: 我们学习阅读只有过去 3000 年的历史。

sentences.en: And in fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: Socrates was concerned that we would lose our ability to remember because sound and memory are very, very, very, very closely tied.
sentences.zh: 苏格拉底曾担心我们会失去记忆能力，因为声音和记忆是紧密相连的。

sentences.en: But first of all, we have to make sound to meaning connections when we learn to talk.
sentences.zh: 但首先，当我们学习说话时，我们必须建立声音与意义的联系。

sentences.en: So that's the first thing that happens.
sentences.zh: 所以这是发生的第一件事。

sentences.en: And then if we have made strong sound to meaning connections, then it will be easier for a child or anyone to connect the sounds with a symbol on a page, a letter.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果我们建立了牢固的声音与意义的联系，那么孩子或任何人将声音与页面上的符号（字母）联系起来就会更容易。

sentences.en: And we can measure sound processing in the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们可以测量大脑中的声音处理过程。

sentences.en: So as I'm talking to you now, the neurons in your brain that respond to sound are producing electricity.
sentences.zh: 所以当我跟你说话时，你大脑中对声音做出反应的神经元正在产生电流。

sentences.en: And with some scalp electrodes, we can measure your brain's response to sound.
sentences.zh: 通过一些头皮电极，我们可以测量你大脑对声音的反应。

sentences.en: And we can figure out how good a job your brain is doing at processing all those different sound ingredients that I spoke of, pitch, timing, timbre, phase.
sentences.zh: 我们可以弄清楚你的大脑在处理我所说的所有那些不同声音成分（音高、时间、音色、相位）方面做得有多好。

sentences.en: And we can see where are the strengths, where are the bottlenecks.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到哪些是优势，哪些是瓶颈。

sentences.en: And we can see that in children who have difficulty reading and who have delayed language skills, we typically see that aspects of
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，在有阅读困难和语言技能延迟的儿童中，我们通常会看到

sentences.en: timing and of the processing of the harmonics, which of course really do enable us to distinguish one consonant from another.
sentences.zh: 时间以及谐波处理方面的表现，而谐波确实使我们能够区分一个辅音和另一个辅音。

sentences.en: I use the metaphor of the brain is mixing board.
sentences.zh: 我用大脑是调音台来做比喻。

sentences.en: So imagine, you know, this, this complex sound that has all the different ingredients is coming into your head.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，这种包含所有不同成分的复杂声音进入你的大脑。

sentences.en: And then your brain is a mixing board where the faders go up and down on these different ingredients, pitch, timing, and timbre.
sentences.zh: 然后你的大脑就是一个调音台，推子在这些不同的成分（音高、时间、音色）上上下移动。

sentences.en: And if you have difficulty reading, the slider, the fader on the harmonics, fader is going to be low.
sentences.zh: 如果你有阅读困难，谐波的推子就会很低。

sentences.en: And certain aspects of timing is going to be low.
sentences.zh: 而某些时间方面的推子也会很低。

sentences.en: And so we can see, oh, there actually is a bottleneck, you know, but all you can see is, oh, here's a child who has difficulty learning to read.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以看到，哦，确实存在一个瓶颈，你知道，但你所能看到的只是，哦，这是一个有学习阅读困难的孩子。

sentences.en: You don't know what's going, what's up with them.
sentences.zh: 你不知道他们出了什么问题。

sentences.en: If you measure their sound processing, you can see well, actually, there's nothing wrong with their sound processing, everything's perfect.
sentences.zh: 如果你测量他们的声音处理能力，你会发现，其实他们的声音处理没有任何问题，一切都很完美。

sentences.en: Or you can see, well, you know, there really are some bottlenecks.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以看到，嗯，确实存在一些瓶颈。

sentences.en: And that can guide us in many ways.
sentences.zh: 这可以在很多方面指导我们。

sentences.en: So what happens with people who are congenitally deaf?
sentences.zh: 那么先天性耳聋的人会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Then how do they learn to read?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何学习阅读的？

sentences.en: Does their brain have to work in a different way?
sentences.zh: 他们的大脑是否必须以不同的方式工作？

sentences.en: Yeah, it can work in a different way.
sentences.zh: 是的，它可以以不同的方式工作。

sentences.en: And now many people who are congenitally deaf get cochlear implants.
sentences.zh: 现在许多先天性耳聋的人会植入人工耳蜗。

sentences.en: Which enable them to actually bypass the ear and stimulate the hearing nerve, stimulate the brain directly, but they're still getting information from sound.
sentences.zh: 这使他们能够绕过耳朵，直接刺激听神经，直接刺激大脑，但他们仍然从声音中获取信息。

sentences.en: So they're still making the same sound to meaning connections and would learn reading in much the same way.
sentences.zh: 所以他们仍然在建立同样的声音与意义的联系，并以同样的方式学习阅读。

sentences.en: That said, if a person is not hearing at all, if they really are born congenitally deaf and they remain deaf, we know that the brain is remarkably plastic and able to
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，如果一个人完全听不见，如果他们确实是先天性耳聋并且一直保持耳聋，我们知道大脑具有极强的可塑性，能够

sentences.en: change based on what inputs it's getting.
sentences.zh: 根据它接收到的输入进行改变。

sentences.en: So that if the sonic inputs are non-existent, then other parts of the
sentences.zh: 所以如果声音输入不存在，那么大脑的其他部分

sentences.en: brain will develop and will, you know, become stronger and learning to read and learning many other things can be done through these other channels.
sentences.zh: 就会发育并变得更强，学习阅读和学习许多其他事情可以通过这些其他渠道完成。

sentences.en: And then if you put electrodes on the head of somebody who's congenitally deaf and, you know, trying to understand what it is that
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你在先天性耳聋的人头上放置电极，试图了解他们正在处理什么，

sentences.en: they're processing, I mean, do you get some kind of reading?
sentences.zh: 你会得到某种读数吗？

sentences.en: Because I've seen the readings that you get from people who, two people hear the same thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我见过你从两个人听到同样东西时得到的读数。

sentences.en: I think you've got the example of, um, a Beatles song that's being played for two people and then you can play back what it is that they, they've actually heard.
sentences.zh: 我想你有一个例子，播放一首披头士乐队的歌给两个人听，然后你可以回放他们实际听到的内容。

sentences.en: And it's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这太了不起了。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds just like the Beatles, but what do you get if you're dealing with somebody who really does not hear?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来就像披头士乐队，但如果你面对的是一个真正听不见的人，你会得到什么？

sentences.en: Well, we haven't done that experiment and it's probably one we, we should do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还没有做过那个实验，这可能是我们应该做的。

sentences.en: Um, we, we have, um, done actually quite a bit of work in people who are hearing impaired.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们实际上在听力受损的人身上做了相当多的工作。

sentences.en: So we can see that the people who have a significant hearing loss, um, and especially one that they've acquired throughout their life,
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以看到，那些有严重听力损失的人，尤其是那些在生活中逐渐获得听力损失的人，

sentences.en: they have learned because the hearing brain, the hearing brain is vast and we can see people.
sentences.zh: 他们已经学会了，因为听觉大脑是广阔的，我们可以观察到人们。

sentences.en: I mean, just last week we had a, uh, an 86 year old musician with a very severe, uh, hearing loss in both of his years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就在上周，我们有一位 86 岁的音乐家，他的双耳听力损失非常严重。

sentences.en: And his sound processing was remarkably excellent.
sentences.zh: 而他的声音处理能力非常出色。

sentences.en: Um, because then, and here's the thing, the hearing brain is vaSt. So the hearing brain engages how we think, how we feel, what we know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为，这就是重点，听觉大脑是广阔的。所以听觉大脑涉及我们的思考、感受、所知、

sentences.en: what we remember, what we pay attention to, how we integrate our other senses.
sentences.zh: 所记、所关注的内容，以及我们如何整合其他感官。

sentences.en: So this is the hearing brain.
sentences.zh: 这就是听觉大脑。

sentences.en: This is the brain that responds to vibrations and, and, you know, and think, think of Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 这是对振动做出反应的大脑，想想贝多芬。

sentences.en: Beethoven was deaf and composed some of the very best music that we have in our world
sentences.zh: 贝多芬是聋子，却创作了我们世界上一些最伟大的音乐，

sentences.en: because, uh, the hearing brain is vaSt. The hearing brain is vaSt. And this is, it's counter to the way many people think about the senses.
sentences.zh: 因为听觉大脑是广阔的。听觉大脑是广阔的。这与许多人对感官的看法背道而驰。

sentences.en: They think about the senses as being these parallel things.
sentences.zh: 他们认为感官是这些平行的东西。

sentences.en: They think about, um, you know, what we know, how we feel, uh, even our, our, our, our, our psychological state,
sentences.zh: 他们认为，你知道，我们所知道的、我们的感受，甚至我们的心理状态，

sentences.en: all of that, um, is really part of how we sense the world and how the hearing brain in particular
sentences.zh: 所有这些实际上都是我们感知世界方式的一部分，尤其是听觉大脑

sentences.en: pulls together information from all of these sources in order to make sense of the world.
